resources.string: SafeGit syncs folders such as an Obsidian vault in your phone\'s storage. Git needs to work with them as real files, which takes the \"All files access\" permission.
Connect a folder to a git repo to start syncing it.
Waiting for Android to start the sync…
No changes on this phone to sync
Sync stopped before it finished. Nothing was lost, and the next sync picks up where this one left off.

Both sides changed the same lines. Each of these files now holds both versions, between lines starting with <<<<<<< and >>>>>>>. Edit them to keep what you want, then sync. Nothing is pushed until then.
Both sides changed the same lines of these files. An automatic sync leaves them as they are. Sync to put both versions in each file, then edit it to keep what you want.
These changes can\'t be combined in one file. Choose which version to keep; nothing has changed yet.
Changed on this phone and on the remote
Some files hold both versions between markers. Edit them to keep what you want, then sync.
This phone and the remote changed the same lines. Open SafeGit and sync to see both versions.
Some changes can\'t be combined. Open SafeGit to choose which version to keep.
The remote refused the sign-in. Open SafeGit to sign in again.
Automatic syncs have failed for a day. Open SafeGit to see why.
The repo isn\'t on a branch.
The branch has no remote branch to sync with.
Couldn\'t send changes to the remote.
The remote refused the sign-in, or the repo doesn\'t exist.
The remote kept changing during the sync. Try again.
Files kept changing during the sync. Try again.

An empty folder gets the repo\'s files. A folder that already has notes keeps them, and they merge with the repo\'s on the first sync.
Leave the password or token out of the URL. Sign-in comes separately.
